items.title: Live: Australia rockets to top of Commonwealth Games medal tally
items.description: Lani Pallister wins Australia's first gold of these Commonwealth Games, with her fellow swimmers quickly adding to the tally. Follow live.

items.title: Australia's 'monoculture' might be at the Labor conference
items.description: For those who believe in the virtue of converting and wrangling political trade-offs into a unified, coherent set of messages, Labor's example is transcendent.

items.title: Elder abuse concerns raised as Labor backs VAD telehealth
items.description: A Labor push to lift the ban on accessing voluntary assisted dying through telehealth has triggered a warning about unintended consequences for vulnerable Australians.

items.title: 'End of an era': How the Iran war may change US military strategy
items.description: Five months into a war Donald Trump said would last only weeks, the Iran conflict has so far cost the United States tens of billions of dollars and brought about "the end of an era" in American military strategy.

items.title: Japan's popular princess sparks calls to ditch male-only succession law
items.description: There are only three people in line to inherit Japan's Chrysanthemum Throne, and one of them is 90 years old. All three of them are men.

items.title: India's 'unserious' gen Z are protesting with grit and humour
items.description: Across the country's protest hotspots, India's gen Z are using meme culture as part of their hopes to bring the country into a new dawn.

items.title: Right-wing populist politics is 'extremely anti-women', warns Anna Funder
items.description: The award-winning author, who burst onto the literary scene with her debut, Stasiland, in 2003, discusses writing, AI and the rise of fascism.

items.title: How many jobs will AI data centres create?
items.description: Data centres are in development across Australia, but how many jobs will these big, thirsty facilities actually support?

items.title: Tens of thousands flee fires in France, blazes merge outside Madrid
items.description: France orders total evacuation of Cap Ferret peninsula as Spain declares national emergency for the first time over fires.

items.title: Bali bans two Dutch men alleged to have hosted discriminatory run club
items.description: Bali's Immigration department has banned two Dutch expats from Indonesia for organising a run club event '"fraught with discrimination against local residents".

items.title: Defence minister confirms former senior naval officer faces court martial
items.description: A former senior naval officer will face charges in a military trial set down for up to six weeks from September 14 with the military court ordering their identity remain suppressed.

items.title: New Trump tariffs 'make it harder for Australian businesses to compete'
items.description: The Business Council of Australia says a new tariff will make it harder for Australian businesses to compete in the US and could reduce investment.

items.title: Brewery uses solar bitcoin rig to make beer and cover power bills
items.description: A brewery is using a bitcoin mine to heat the water used in beer production as a way to use up surplus energy generated by rooftop solar panels.

items.title: Guerilla garden removed from Sydney intersection dubbed 'triangle of shame'
items.description: A community group wanted to spark a conversation about greening a concrete strip but drew the ire of transport authorities.

items.title: ABC 5050 quiz: Testing your knowledge of L7's biggest hit, the Odyssey and rainbows made of fog
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: The UK is banning high-caffeine drinks for under-16s. How does coffee compare?
items.description: The British government wants to ban the sale of high-caffeine energy drinks to people under the age of 16. But how do they compare to coffee, tea and other beverages many people regularly consume? And what's the situation here in Austalia?

items.title: Farmers kept planting as the war raged and now they are paying for it
items.description: North Queensland farmers urge consumers to eat more vegetables as rising costs and low demand create a "perfect storm".

items.title: Islanders sang hymns and kept vigil over body of teenager washed ashore
items.description: Twenty-seven people including families with young children went missing after two boats capsized in rough seas in Papua New Guinea's north-east on Saturday.

items.title: Twin thrillers and key injuries in crazy NRL double-header
items.description: Dylan Lucas, Dylan Brown and Harry Grant are all set for stints on the sidelines after the star trio were all injured across two NRL thrillers on Friday night.

items.title: Cats down Dees, Dockers flex muscle against Eagles in derby
items.description: Geelong ends Melbourne's MCG winning streak with a crucial scalp to keep touch with the top six, while Fremantle strolls to derby victory over West Coast.

items.title: New report reveals what triggered SA's catastrophic algal bloom crisis
items.description: A new report reveals what caused South Australia's most devastating algal bloom crisis — 18 months after it first appeared on the state's waters.

items.title: Four regional RSLs merge to keep veterans' services going
items.description: While RSLs across Victoria grapple with declining numbers and increased administration, sub-branches in Sunraysia are forging their own path.

items.title: Adolescence creator tackles teen rehab very differently in The Good Boy
items.description: Emmy Award-winning Adolescence co-creator Stephen Graham tackles teen delinquency in a very different way in The Good Boy.

items.title: Russian missile strike kills 10 at Ukraine defence industry event
items.description: A Russian ballistic missile strike has killed 10 people and injured almost 100 at a defence industry event near Kyiv, as the Kremlin says it will keep fighting while awaiting new US peace proposals.

items.title: Singer Chris Brown pleads guilty to affray over London nightclub incident
items.description: US singer Chris Brown has pleaded guilty to affray over an altercation in a London nightclub in a fight that injured a music producer with a glass bottle.
